text:
incident-bot: PAGER — sev=high — possible cross-tenant response exposure detected in dedicated pool 'dedicated-eu-west-2'. Affected tenant: NovaHealth (enterprise-vpc). 50 requests in the last 10m with mismatched tenant headers. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tenant-isolation|tenant-isolation>. Paging on-call.

oncall-sre (alex): ack — picking this up. tagging eng-runtime and eng-infra. first step: confirm impact window and whether responses contain other tenants' IDs.

eng-runtime (maya): seeing traces where x-tenant-id in request != x-tenant-id in response metadata. quick log grep (masked):
```
2026-03-14T21:05:12Z request_id=abc123 tenant_req=novahealth backend_tenant=zenora model=redwood-large status=200
2026-03-14T21:05:13Z request_id=def456 tenant_req=zenora backend_tenant=novahealth model=redwood-large status=200
```
It looks like two tenant IDs swapped in the response metadata for different requests. Not seeing obvious errors in model code.

eng-infra (kyle): checking routing layer (envoy) for overlapping route prefixes. Pulled current route table diff from last config deploy:
```
- match: prefix "/t/novahealth/"
- route: cluster nou-pool
+ match: prefix "/t/"
+ route: cluster shared-dedicated
```
There's a change from a per-tenant prefix to a catch-all /t/ in the last deploy (commit 6f4a2c9). That could cause wrong routing when KV-based tenant isolation assumed prefix.

oncall-sre (alex): ok — that's actionable. Maya, can you assert whether KV cache keys are being indexed by prefix or tenant header? If cache keys ignore tenant header, we could be returning cached responses across tenants.

eng-runtime (maya): confirmed — cache key generation uses request.path + model_id. It does NOT include x-tenant-id in current build. Evidence:
```
# from runtime config
cache_key: "{request.path}:{model_id}"
# samples of cache store keys
/t/novahealth/predict:redwood-large -> <cached response A>
/t/zenora/predict:redwood-large -> <cached response B>
# but because route collapsed to /t/ both requests hit same internal cache shard
```

eng-security (sam): stop any additional writes to shared cache shard. Preserve logs and memcache dump for forensics. Legal/compliance notified (NovaHealth has strict data rules).

oncall-sre (alex): mitigation plan: 1) flip routing back to per-tenant prefixes (rollback the route change) 2) invalidate cache shard(s) for dedicated-eu-west-2 3) isolate NovaHealth's pool (drain traffic) 4) inform customer and open incident ticket. Anyone opposed?

infra-bot: Starting run: route rollback -> applying config from commit 6f4a2b8 (pre-change). Command: 
```
redwoodctl config apply --env prod --file configs/routes/2026-03-14/pre-prefix-collapse.yaml --dry-run=false
```
Result: queued, will take ~45s to propagate to edge.

customer-success (tara): contacting NovaHealth SOC now with high-level notice: "We have detected potential cross-tenant metadata leakage. We're mitigating and will provide timeline and next steps." They asked for impacted request window and whether any PII might have been included.

devops (jess): preparing cache invalidation. Commands to run on memcached cluster (masked):
```
# targeted invalidation
memcc flush --servers ded-eu-2-cache-1,ded-eu-2-cache-2 --prefix "/t/" --confirm
# or per-tenant
memcc delete --key "/t/novahealth/predict:redwood-large"
```
Note: full flush will be disruptive to latency for that pool for ~2m while caches warm. Recommend targeted deletes if we can enumerate keys.

eng-runtime (maya): grabbing memcache dump and will snapshot /var/run/kv-cache before invalidation. Sample showing cross-tenant entries (IDs masked):
```
key: /t/novahealth/predict:redwood-large -> response.headers.x-tenant-id: zenora
key: /t/zenora/predict:redwood-large    -> response.headers.x-tenant-id: novahealth
```
That's consistent with route collapse + cache key lacking tenant header.

oncall-sre (alex): infra-bot reports route rollback succeeded at ts=1880012550. eng-infra/kyle please confirm that Envoy configs on all edges have reverted and that we have per-tenant route matches again.

eng-infra (kyle): confirmed — propagated to 6/6 edges. Verifying with `curl` tests hitting dedicated pool:
```
curl -H "x-tenant-id: novahealth" https://ded-eu-west-2.internal/t/novahealth/predict | jq .meta.tenant
"novahealth"
curl -H "x-tenant-id: zenora"  https://ded-eu-west-2.internal/t/zenora/predict    | jq .meta.tenant
"zenora"
```

oncall-sre (alex): cache invalidation in progress. jess, after targeted invalidation, can you keep TTLs low for the next 2h? We'll want to avoid immediate re-population with stale behavior while engineers ship a fix to include tenant in cache keys.

devops (jess): done with targeted deletes. Reduced cache TTL to 30s for dedicated-eu-west-2. Commands executed at ts=1880012705.

eng-runtime (maya): beginning code fix to include x-tenant-id in cache key and adding a regression test. Patch id: fe12a9c. Will push to canary tonight; request rollback window if any failures.

eng-security (sam): preserving evidence: memcache dump uploaded to s3://incidents/evidence/1880012345/ (access log saved). Please do not purge. Legal asked to be CCed on communications.

customer-success (tara): NovaHealth acknowledges mitigation and requests a timeline for full fix, any data access audit, and an incident call. I'm scheduling a bridging call in 30m.

compliance-bot: Reminder — create an incident ticket with classification 'potential cross-tenant exposure' and set retention to 3 years. Suggested S3 path: s3://incidents/retention/1880012345-novahealth.

oncall-sre (alex): current status: rollback complete, targeted cache invalidation done, pool isolated while runtime patch is prepared, customer notified. Impact: potential metadata leakage observed in ~50 requests (investigation ongoing). Escalating to oncall handoff: night oncall @oncall-night (samira) will take over at 23:00 UTC with runbook steps and follow-up action items.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1880012345. Link: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-1880012345>. Pager status -> acknowledged.

oncall-sre (alex): assigning follow-ups: 
- eng-runtime (maya): ship patch to include tenant in cache_key + regression tests (target: 02:00 UTC)
- eng-infra (kyle): add automated check to prevent prefix-collapse in routing configs (PR: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pull/412)
- eng-security (sam): lead audit of which responses contained mismatched tenant metadata, coordinate with legal.
- customer-success (tara): run customer call and update timeline.

devops (jess): leaving note: snapshot path for memcache and configs: s3://incidents/evidence/1880012345/memcache-snap.tar.gz (sha256: masked).

oncall-sre (alex): handing off to night oncall. I'll post a short summary to the incident ticket and start a postmortem template after resolution. If anything changes before handoff, I will update.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded. New assignee: oncall-night (samira).

eng-runtime (maya): quick note before handoff — root cause hypothesis: recent routing config change collapsed per-tenant path into a shared prefix; runtime cache keys omitted tenant identifier, enabling cross-tenant cache hits. Fixes: revert routing (done), invalidate caches (done), add tenant to cache key (in progress), add gating test to CI for route-prefix parity (planned).

oncall-sre (alex): thanks team. Keep logs/timestamps in ticket. Postmortem will include timeline, blast radius, and customer impact.

customer-success (tara): NovaHealth confirmed no PII was present in the leaked responses per initial scan but requested full audit. Will keep them informed.

incident-bot: Closing thread: mitigation in place, patch in progress, customer engaged. Incident remains open until validation and postmortem complete.
